== Biography ==
William Glasgow, gamekeeper to the Earl of Hopetoun, is identified with the family commemorated in the held Crawford and Leadhills memorial derivatives. Both give his death on 26 April 1853, but differ between ages 74 and 71; neither is preferred here. His wife Janet Thomson and the family dates are discussed below. The cemetery labels are source descriptions, not proof of multiple interments.<ref name="CrawfordMemorial" /><ref name="LeadhillsVariant" />

== Research Notes ==
=== Leadhills companion memorial: age conflict — 4 November 2026 ===

The newly inspected Leadhills derivative names William Glasgow, gamekeeper to the Earl of Hopetoun, his spouse Janet Thomson and the same family dates as the held Crawford memorial. It gives William’s death as 26 April 1853, aged 71; the existing Crawford rendering gives the same date but age 74. These imply approximate births around 1782 and 1779 respectively, not independently recorded birthdays. The matching occupation, spouse, death dates and children identify companion renderings of the same family memorial; they are not independent witnesses and do not resolve the age disagreement. Both readings are retained without changing vital fields.<ref name="LeadhillsVariant">Findmypast, Scotland Monumental Inscriptions, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBPRS%2FSCOT%2FMIS%2F511339 William Glasgow, Leadhills Cemetery, GBPRS/SCOT/MIS/511339], derivative transcript inspected 4 November 2026, original monument uninspected. Companion to [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00557896&tab=this Crawford memorial PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00557896], existing canonical record crawford-william-gamekeeper-memorial-1853 and source s-5c22ecf3b0e8489c, reused without recapture.</ref>

The new text gives Janet’s death as 1 April 1845, aged 62; calls John, James and George three of her children; says John and James died in infancy; and gives George’s death as 21 July 1816, aged 7. It also commemorates Isabel Glasgow, died 27 November 1881, aged 73, without expressly calling her a daughter. Her daughter identification rests on the existing baptism and household context rather than that literal line alone. The reported surname Thomson does not independently establish maiden-name wording. No new spouse, child or mother is attached.

Leadhills Cemetery is the new provider’s cemetery label; the older source is indexed at Crawford and the inherited biography combined Crawford Old Churchyard and Leadhills Cemetery. These labels do not prove two burial places or establish every commemorated person’s actual interment. The original inscription or photograph remains uninspected and is needed to settle age and cemetery precision.

George Glasgow-638 remains the later child comparison only. His held birth on 8 June 1818 is after the memorial George’s death on 21 July 1816, so he cannot be that deceased child. The existing proposed William Glasgow-2715 father attachment remains probable at 88%, including the unresolved Crawford-child to Leicester-adult identity. No new support percentage is gained from a companion index. The original 1843 Leicester marriage father and occupation fields remain the discriminating test; the older George’s 1810 baptism versus reported age 7 in 1816 also remains unresolved.

=== Preserved earlier opening ===

The following original opening is retained as source and proposal history. Its unqualified age, locality, interment or adult-identity wording is qualified by the account above; no source is withdrawn.

The inscription found in Crawford Old Churchyard and Leadhills Cemetery in Crawford, Lanarkshire, Scotland, commemorates various members of the Glasgow family. Specifically, the inscription pays tribute to William Glasgow, who served as a gamekeeper to the Right Honourable Earl of Hopetoun, noting his passing on April 26, 1853, at the age of 74. Additionally, the inscription memorializes his wife, Janet Thomson, who passed away on April 1, 1845, at the age of 62. The inscription also mentions three of their children: John and James, who died in infancy, and George, who passed away at the age of 7 on July 21, 1816. Lastly, the inscription remembers Isabel Glasgow, who passed away on November 27, 1881, at the age of 73. This commemorative inscription is documented within the Scotland Monumental Inscriptions collection, a subset of the Birth, Marriage, Death & Parish Records category. It provides insights into the lives and familial connections of those interred in the Crawford Old Churchyard and Leadhills Cemetery, contributing to the historical records of the area.


=== Possible William Allen Glasgow, Royal Engineers commission, 1795 ===
Gentleman Cadet William Allen Glasgow is announced as second lieutenant in the Corps of Royal Engineers, vice Lefebvre, promoted, dated 1 October 1795.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395720951/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1795-10-15, p.4].</ref>

The commission date is 1 October 1795, not the 15 October publication day. "Gentleman Cadet" describes his prior status; the notice gives no parents, birthplace or subsequent career. A William without a recorded middle name remains a possible identification.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2715]]. Estimated c. 1779 Crawford birth is compatible with a young cadet. Estimated age and a missing middle name do not exclude him; no engineering-service connection.


=== Crawford family connection — 31 October 2026 ===

George Glasgow-638 is already described in his held and live biography as the Crawford child of William Glasgow and Janet Thomson, but neither parent profile is attached. The inspected Scotland baptism index names that exact couple for George, born 8 June 1818 and baptised 14 June at Crawford. An exact-parent search returned thirteen Crawford entries spanning 1802–1828, including Isabel in 1808 and an older George in 1810. The inspected monumental-inscription transcript identifies William Glasgow-2715, gamekeeper to the Earl of Hopetoun, his wife Janet Thomson, their daughter Isabel (died 1881 aged 73), and an older George who died in July 1816. The 1841 census transcript places gamekeeper William with Janet and Isabella at Hass, Crawford; the 1851 transcript gives widower William, 72, born Crawford, with daughter Isabella and younger children. This combination supports the gamekeeper as the 1818 child’s father, with reuse of the deceased child’s name. The proposed attachment to the later Leicester adult is assessed at 88% subjective confidence, including the unresolved childhood-to-adult identification.<ref name="Crawford1818">FamilySearch, [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTLF-1QX Scotland Births and Baptisms, George Glasgow], birth 8 June/baptism 14 June 1818, Crawford, William Glasgow and Janet Thomson, source detail 2:15KCJHH. Original unavailable in inspected view; [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=R_685665034&tab=this Findmypast R_685665034] reproduces the same index.</ref><ref name="CrawfordMemorial">Scottish Genealogy Society, Scotland Monumental Inscriptions, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=PRS%2FSCOTLAND%2FMI%2FADD%2F5%2F00557896&tab=this William Glasgow, Crawford], Findmypast PRS/SCOTLAND/MI/ADD/5/00557896. Provider transcript inspected 31 October 2026; gravestone image uninspected.</ref><ref name="CrawfordCensus">Findmypast, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBC/1841/0017061572&expand=true 1841 census GBC/1841/0017061572] and [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=GBC/1851/0019486912&expand=true 1851 census GBC/1851/0019486912], Hass, Crawford, William Glasgow gamekeeper and household. Provider transcripts inspected 31 October 2026; originals uninspected.</ref>

The baptism and census originals and gravestone image have not been inspected; these are provider index/transcript readings. FamilySearch and Findmypast reproduce the same underlying baptism index and are not independent evidence. The later Leicester adult’s exact birthday may derive from the baptism, so it is not counted as independent confirmation. His inspected 1843 GRO marriage index locates a Leicester entry with Mary Ann Norton among the same-page spouse possibilities, but gives no father or father’s occupation. The original marriage is the decisive next test. The memorial’s older George, died 1816 aged 7, cannot be the 1818 child; its reported age differs by about a year from the 1810 baptism and remains unresolved. Some sibling index birth fields contain malformed years and the 1806 John dates conflict; none is silently corrected. William Glasgow-1533, the circa-1795 Glasgow-born weaver with a Janet Thomson wife, remains a distinct comparison rather than being excluded merely for missing fields: the gamekeeper’s 1841/1851 Crawford household, older age, trade, wife and Isabel chronology provide the positive match. No exact vital replacement, mother attachment, profile merger or upstream father is inferred.<ref name="Leicester1843">England and Wales marriages 1837–2005, George Glasgow, Leicester, Q3 1843, volume 15, page 158, [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=BMD%2FM%2F1843%2F3%2FAZ%2F000191%2F137&tab=this Findmypast GRO index]. Mary Ann Norton is a same-page spouse possibility. This is not a marriage certificate or a father clause.</ref>

Proposed family amendment: add [[Glasgow-2715|William Glasgow]], Crawford gamekeeper, as father of [[Glasgow-638|George Glasgow]], probable at 88%. No live WikiTree save has been made.

=== Withdrawn engineer comparison ===

The old William Allen Glasgow Royal Engineers comparison is withdrawn. The dated 6 October review records the engineer’s death at Martinique in 1798, incompatible with this gamekeeper’s 1841/1851 census household and 1853 memorial. The 17 October text repeated an earlier candidate and does not restore that identity. No military career is assigned to the Crawford gamekeeper.
